name: What is the difference between porcelain and marble wall tile for bathrooms?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between porcelain and marble wall tile for bathrooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ceramic and porcelain are manufactured, glazed tiles, while marble is a natural, porous stone. Ceramic and porcelain offer superior stain and moisture resistance with minimal maintenance, making them ideal for high-use family showers. Marble delivers a unique, upscale look with natural veining, but it requires regular sealing and pH-neutral cleaners to avoid etching. Marble also demands precise diamond-blade cutting and careful setting so mortar does not shadow through lighter slabs. If low maintenance is your top priority, porcelain provides an easier long-term ownership experience.
acceptedAnswer.description: Porcelain is non-porous, highly water-resistant, and low-maintenance. Marble provides a high-end natural aesthetic but requires regular sealing and careful cleaning to prevent stains.
